Ten men were healed. Only one came back to say thank you. 🙏 Luke 17

Ten lepers “stood afar off” and cried, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.” He sent them to the priests, “and it came to pass, that, as they went, they were cleansed.” One of them turned back, fell at His feet “giving him thanks: and he was a Samaritan.” Jesus asked: “Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?” (Luke 17:12-17)

Happy Thanksgiving! What's one thing you're thanking God for today? 👇

An army surrounded them. Then God opened his eyes. 🔥 2 Kings 6

The king of Syria sent “horses, and chariots, and a great host” by night to surround Elisha. His servant panicked: “Alas, my master! how shall we do?” Elisha said, “Fear not: for they that be with us are more than they that be with them.” Then he prayed, and “the mountain was full of horses and chariots of fire round about Elisha” (2 Kings 6:14-17).

What are you facing that feels bigger than you? Drop a 🔥 if you needed this today 👇

Moses' face was glowing and he had no idea. It's in the Bible. ✨

Hidden details #6: Moses “wist not that the skin of his face shone” (Exodus 34:29), Israel's shoes didn't wear out in 40 years (Deuteronomy 29:5), Enoch “was not; for God took him” (Genesis 5:24), Jesus wrote on the ground with His finger (John 8:6), and the servant whose ear Peter cut off was named Malchus (John 18:10).

Which one did you already know? Comment 1 to 5 👇

They prayed all night for a miracle. Then they didn't open the door. 😅 Acts 12

Herod put Peter in prison, “but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.” An angel woke him, “his chains fell off from his hands,” and the iron gate “opened to them of his own accord.” Peter knocked at the house where they were praying. Rhoda was so glad she “opened not the gate for gladness.” They told her, “Thou art mad.” (Acts 12:5-15)

Be honest: have you ever been surprised when God answered your prayer? 👇

A huge army was coming. So the king sent the singers out first. 🎶 2 Chronicles 20

King Jehoshaphat prayed, “we have no might against this great company… neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.” God answered: “the battle is not yours, but God's.” So he appointed singers to go out before the army, saying, “Praise the Lord; for his mercy endureth for ever.” “And when they began to sing and to praise, the Lord set ambushments.” (2 Chronicles 20:12-22)

Happy Thanksgiving! Drop your go-to worship song for tonight 👇
